an5.49:1.1: On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park.
an5.49:1.2: Then King Pasenadi of Kosala approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, and sat down to one side.
an5.49:2.1: Now on that occasion Queen Mallikā had just died.
an5.49:2.2: Then a man approached King Pasendi and whispered in his ear:
an5.49:2.4: When this was said, King Pasenadi was pained and saddened, and he sat there with slumping shoulders, facing downward, glum, and speechless.
an5.49:3.1: Then the Blessed One, having known the king’s condition, said to him:
an5.49:3.2: “Great king, there are these five situations that are unobtainable by an ascetic or a brahmin, by a deva, Māra, or Brahmā, or by anyone in the world.”
an5.49:3.3: The rest of this sutta is identical with 5:48,
